docs.title: Delivery Team Plugin
docs.text:
A full delivery pipeline for Claude Code with 11 specialized skills, a 7-stage pipeline, 6 collaboration patterns, and 13 alias themes.

The delivery-team plugin coordinates an AI delivery team through structured stages — from idea capture through user acceptance testing — with self-correction loops, adversarial review, and self-learning memory.

docs.title: At a Glance
docs.text: Feature Details Skills 11 specialized roles (PO, Developer, Architect, QA, and more) Pipeline Stages 7 stages: Idea, Refine, Design, Architect, Plan, Development, UAT Project Types 6 types with automatic detection and stage routing Collaboration Patterns 6 patterns including adversarial review and debate Alias Themes 13 built-in character themes (Lord of the Rings, Star Wars, etc.) Self-Learning Memory Tiered chunked retrieval that improves with every run Quality Gates Team Definition of Done with multi-role validation

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Start the pipeline — Say "start a new feature" to trigger delivery-team:delivery-flow
  2. Setup wizard — The wizard auto-detects your project and generates .delivery/config.yml
  3. Pipeline execution — The orchestrator routes work through stages, invoking specialized skills as sub-agents
  4. Quality gates — Each stage is validated by multiple team roles before advancing
  5. Self-correction — When validation fails, the pipeline routes feedback back to the responsible agent (max 3 iterations)
  6. Memory — Lessons from every run are stored and applied to future runs

Each skill operates as an isolated sub-agent — it receives only the artifacts and context relevant to its task, produces its output, and returns a signal to the orchestrator. The orchestrator never reads artifact content directly; it passes file paths between agents.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: The delivery-team plugin is built on a few core architectural patterns.

docs.title: Pipeline Architecture
docs.text:
The delivery pipeline follows a delegation, not execution model:

  • The orchestrator (delivery-flow) manages flow, routing, and validation
  • Worker skills (developer, architect, quality, etc.) produce all artifacts
  • Workers are invoked as sub-agents using the Agent tool with isolated context

docs.title: Two-Channel Communication
docs.text:
Channel Content Flow Signal STATUS, file paths, summaries (<200 chars) Through orchestrator for routing Artifact File contents (any length) Written to disk by sub-agents

The orchestrator passes file paths between agents, never artifact content. If information is longer than 200 characters, it belongs in a file.

docs.title: Context Isolation
docs.text:
Each sub-agent receives only:

  • Upstream artifact file paths (not content — it reads them from disk)
  • Memory lessons relevant to its task
  • Its own SKILL.md and reference files
  • Alias personality block (if theme is active)

No agent sees the full pipeline state. No agent sees another agent's reasoning.

docs.title: Artifact Flow
docs.text:
Artifacts follow a namespaced convention:

.delivery/artifacts/{NN}-{stage-name}/{role}/{artifact-name}.md

Each sub-agent writes to its own dedicated directory. No two agents share a write path. The orchestrator writes only to stage-summary.md (metadata) and .delivery/state.md (pipeline state).

docs.title: Stage-to-Stage Contracts
docs.text:
Each stage transition has defined contracts specifying required output sections. The downstream stage validates its inputs before starting work.

Transition Key Artifact Required Sections Idea to Refine 01-idea/po/idea-brief.md Problem Statement, Target Users, Goals Refine to Design 02-refine/po/prd.md Personas, Stories with ACs Design to Architect 03-design/ux/design.md User flows, wireframes Architect to Plan 04-architect/architect/architecture.md Components, data models, ADRs Plan to Dev 05-plan/sm/sprint-plan.md Tasks, test cases, dependencies Dev to UAT 06-dev/developer/*.md Implementation per story

docs.title: Feature Knowledge System
docs.text:
Every delivered feature gets a Feature Knowledge Card (FKC) at .delivery/features/<feature-slug>.md. Cards track:

  • What the feature provides (interfaces, contracts)
  • What it consumes (dependencies, assumptions)
  • Data profile (storage, access patterns, volume)
  • Operations concerns (config keys, migrations, deployment dependencies)
  • Known fragilities and boundary tests

The Impact Analysis Gate runs before architecture decisions to check existing FKCs for potential conflicts.

docs.title: Self-Learning Memory
docs.text:
Memory uses a tiered chunked system. See the Memory System reference for full details.

Key design decisions:

  • Routing index (~50 lines) is the only file read on every pipeline start
  • Stage chunks (~100 lines each) are loaded per-stage, not upfront
  • Topic chunks are loaded based on context (checkpoints, decisions, gate failures)
  • Run archives are preserved but never loaded during normal execution

docs.title: Pipeline State Persistence
docs.text:
Pipeline state is persisted in .delivery/state.md as YAML frontmatter. On session interruption:

  • Resume: Load state, skip completed stages, continue from current stage
  • Restart: Archive old state, start fresh
  • Config divergence: If config changed since pipeline started, warn and offer restart

docs.title: Defect Tracking
docs.text:
The pipeline tracks defect rates per sprint as a quality metric:

  • Target: less than 0.3 defects per story
  • Defect categories reviewed in retrospectives
  • Persistent patterns trigger plugin self-improvement PRs
  • Rate trends monitored over time

docs.title: Git and GitHub Integration
docs.text:
The pipeline integrates with Git for branching, commits, and PRs:

  • Branching: trunk-based, github-flow, or gitflow (configurable)
  • Commits: Conventional commit messages with issue linking
  • Issues: Auto-create GitHub issues from user stories at Refine
  • PRs: Auto-create PR at UAT stage
  • Branch naming: <type>/<issue-number>-<short-description>

docs.title: Required Development Skills
docs.text:
Use plugin-dev skills

When modifying this repo, always use the relevant plugin-dev skill:

  • Creating/modifying hooks: load plugin-dev:hook-development first
  • Creating/modifying skills: load plugin-dev:skill-development first
  • Creating/modifying plugin structure: load plugin-dev:plugin-structure first
  • After creating a skill: use plugin-dev:skill-reviewer to review it
  • After creating a plugin: use plugin-dev:plugin-validator to validate it

docs.title: SKILL.md Files
docs.text:
Each skill has a SKILL.md file that serves as the primary instruction set. These files contain:

  • Skill metadata (frontmatter with name, description, license)
  • Design principles (context isolation, role detection)
  • Phase protocols (detection, sub-agent invocation)
  • Task type routing tables
  • Output contracts and patterns
  • Reference file mappings
  • User commands

docs.title: Reference Files
docs.text:
Reference files contain domain-specific knowledge loaded on demand. Key rules:

  • Sub-agents load only the references relevant to their task
  • Never load all reference files into a single context
  • Reference files are the single source of truth for domain knowledge

docs.title: Config Schema
docs.text:
The single source of truth for .delivery/config.yml format is delivery-flow/references/config-schema.md (currently v2.7).

When adding new config keys, follow the extension protocol:

  1. Add the key to the schema table with type, default, valid values
  2. Bump the version
  3. Add a wizard question if interactive
  4. Add to the pipeline config table in SKILL.md
  5. Add a migration note
  6. Regenerate JSON schema (python delivery-team/scripts/generate-schema.py)
  7. Update the consuming skill

docs.title: Three-Level Context Loading
docs.text:
All skills follow this pattern:

  1. Metadata (always loaded) — from marketplace.json
  2. SKILL.md (loaded when skill triggers) — main instructions
  3. Resources (loaded on demand) — scripts, references, assets

docs.title: Pull Request Process
docs.text:
1. Create a feature branch following the naming convention: feature/<issue>-<description>
  2. Make your changes using the appropriate plugin-dev skills
  3. Test by actually using the modified components (dogfooding)
  4. Create a PR with a clear description of changes

docs.title: Adding a New Skill
docs.text:
1. Create the skill directory: delivery-team/skills/<skill-name>/
  2. Write SKILL.md with frontmatter, design principles, and protocols
  3. Add reference files under references/
  4. Register in the marketplace if applicable
  5. Review with plugin-dev:skill-reviewer
  6. Update this documentation site

docs.title: Adding a New Hook
docs.text:
1. Add the hook definition to delivery-team/hooks/hooks.json
  2. Implement the hook script in delivery-team/hooks/
  3. Test the hook by triggering its event type
  4. Document the hook in the Hooks Reference

docs.title: Adding a New Alias Theme
docs.text:
1. Create delivery-flow/references/aliases/<theme-name>.yml
  2. Map all 13 roles (or mark as partial)
  3. Set personality_strength (light, moderate, full)
  4. Test by setting aliases.theme in config and running the pipeline

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Claude Code CLI installed and authenticated
  • A project directory where you want to use the delivery pipeline

docs.title: Install the Plugin
docs.text:
Install the delivery-team plugin from the Claude Plugins marketplace:

claude plugin install P47Phoenix/Claude-Plugins/delivery-team

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
After installation, start a Claude Code session in your project directory and check that the plugin is available:

delivery-team:delivery-flow

The orchestrator should activate and check for existing configuration. If no .delivery/config.yml exists, it will launch the setup wizard.

docs.title: What Gets Installed
docs.text:
The plugin adds these skills to your Claude Code environment:

The plugin also installs 7 hooks for session management, pipeline enforcement, and quality validation. See the Hooks Reference for details.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Get from zero to a running delivery pipeline in under 5 minutes.

docs.title: Quick-Start Wizard (3 Questions)
docs.text: The full setup wizard asks 9+ questions about your project. Quick-start mode collapses everything into 3 questions. Say "quick start", "quick setup", or "just get started" when the wizard launches.

docs.title: Question 1: What are you building?
docs.text:
Describe your project in one sentence. The wizard auto-detects the project type:

You Say Detected Type "New web app from scratch" GREENFIELD "Adding search to our API" FEATURE "Fix the login crash" BUG_FIX "New roguelike in Godot" GAME_DEV+GREENFIELD "Investigate whether Redis fits" SPIKE "Write API docs" DOCS_ONLY

docs.title: Question 2: What language/framework?
docs.text: The wizard scans your codebase for languages and frameworks. Confirm or correct what it finds. For greenfield projects with no codebase yet, just tell it what you plan to use.

docs.title: Question 3: How strict?
docs.text:
Level What It Means Prototype Minimal gates. Fast. Evaluator-optimizer only. No human checkpoints except UAT. Standard Balanced. Evaluator-optimizer + adversarial review + decision routing. Checkpoints at Refine and UAT. Strict Full ceremony. All 6 collaboration patterns. All 4 checkpoints. All enforcement on.

Everything else uses smart defaults based on your project type and strictness level. You can re-run setup later to fine-tune.

docs.title: Step 1: Start the Pipeline
docs.text:
Say: "start a new feature"

This triggers delivery-team:delivery-flow. The orchestrator checks for existing configuration.

docs.title: Step 2: Quick-Start Wizard
docs.text: If no .delivery/config.yml exists, the wizard launches. Say "quick start" and answer the 3 questions. The wizard generates your config and initializes the .delivery/ directory.

docs.title: Step 3: Idea (Stage 1)
docs.text: Describe your idea in detail. The Product Owner captures it as an idea brief and validates it meets entry criteria.

docs.title: Step 4: Refine (Stage 2)
docs.text: The Product Owner writes a PRD with user stories, acceptance criteria, and scope. If checkpoints are enabled, you review and approve before moving on.

docs.title: Step 5: Design (Stage 3)
docs.text: The UX Designer creates user flows and wireframes. The team reviews for completeness and usability.

docs.title: Step 6: Architect (Stage 4)
docs.text: The Architect designs system architecture — components, data models, API contracts, technology decisions. If checkpoints are enabled, you approve the architecture.

docs.title: Step 7: Plan (Stage 5)
docs.text: The Scrum Master creates a sprint plan with implementable tasks and test cases. If checkpoints are enabled, you approve the plan.

docs.title: Step 8: Development (Stage 6)
docs.text: The Developer implements each story. The QA Engineer reviews against acceptance criteria. Self-correction loops handle issues automatically.

docs.title: Step 9: UAT (Stage 7)
docs.text: User Acceptance Testing runs. Simulated personas test the deliverables. You review the final output and accept or reject. On acceptance, the pipeline completes and writes lessons to memory.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Deliver a full song (title, lyric sheet, chord chart, melody sketch, arrangement notes, production brief) from a one-line brief, through a staged pipeline with quality gates.
  • Mirror the delivery-team architecture so contributors already familiar with delivery-flow can navigate music-flow immediately: one orchestrator, role-scoped worker skills, sub-agents with isolated context, hooks, config, memory.
  • Load song-craft knowledge progressively: genre, role, and task references enter a sub-agent's context only when that sub-agent needs them. Never load the whole craft library at once.
  • Produce machine-checkable artifacts where possible (ABC notation for melody, a structured lyric sheet with section tags, a chord chart in Roman numerals plus concert pitch) so hooks and scripts can validate rather than merely eyeball.
  • Be deterministic at the gates: pass/fail decisions on prosody, rhyme scheme, structure, energy curve, challenger severity, and originality are rule-based (scripts), not vibes.
  • Ship user value early: a lyric-only song is producible end-to-end by the third PR (see §17, story W2-5).

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Audio rendering, mixing, or mastering. The pipeline ends at a production brief plus a MIDI/ABC sketch. DAW work is out of scope.
  • Reproducing or closely imitating specific copyrighted songs or artists' lyrics. See §15.
  • Music-theory tutoring as a primary purpose. Theory references exist to serve the pipeline, not as a standalone course.
  • Replacing delivery-team. music-team is a sibling plugin, not a sub-skill of delivery-flow.
  • Non-English lyrics at v1. The syllable, stress, and rhyme heuristics are English-only. Other languages run the pipeline with those gates reporting SKIPPED, not FAIL. See §12 and §20.

docs.title: 2. Design Principles
docs.text:
These are lifted from delivery-team/references/shared/orchestrator-doctrine.md and adapted.

  1. Orchestrator never writes the song. music-flow coordinates stages and gates. Every lyric line, chord, and melody note is produced by a worker skill running as a sub-agent.
  2. Context isolation by role and genre. A lyricist sub-agent working on a country ballad loads lyricist/references/genres/country.md and nothing about hip-hop. A composer sub-agent for the same song loads composer/references/genres/country.md and nothing about lyrics.
  3. Evaluator-optimizer at every creative stage. A worker produces, a critic evaluates against an explicit rubric, the worker revises. Loop caps are configurable; exhaustion follows the configured escalation policy.
  4. Adversarial re-verification before release. A challenger sub-agent with a clean context attempts to break the song (cliché density, prosody collisions, structural monotony, accidental resemblance to known works) before the final gate.
  5. Deterministic gates. Scripts decide pass/fail on measurable properties. Sub-agents interpret and improve; they never self-certify and never override a gate. Only the user may override, and the override is recorded.
  6. One gate runner. The orchestrator's stage protocol (step 4) is the only place a gate decides a loop. Hooks that run gate scripts are advisory and feed the same result; they never block independently.
  7. Everything on disk. Every stage writes to .song/<song-slug>/ so a session can resume, a retrospective can read it, and memory can learn from it.
  8. Budgeted SKILL.md files. Tier A/B/C line budgets apply exactly as in governance/skill-budgets.json. Depth lives in references/.

docs.title: 3. Progressive Disclosure Model
docs.text:
Four levels, each loaded strictly later than the previous.

Level What loads When Where L0 — Metadata Plugin + skill names, descriptions, trigger phrases Always (marketplace index) .claude-plugin/marketplace.json L1 — Skill body SKILL.md of the triggered skill (orchestrator or worker) When the skill triggers music-team/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md L2 — Role / task reference One role file + one output contract When the worker dispatches a sub-agent for a specific task skills/<skill>/references/roles/, references/contracts/ L3 — Genre / technique reference Genre, technique, persona, or rubric files per the role's allowance Loaded inside the sub-agent prompt only skills/<skill>/references/genres/, techniques/, personas/, rubrics/

Prompt allowance manifest. Each role has an explicit allowance in references/shared/prompt-allowances.json listing which reference directories it may embed and how many files from each. The default allowance for creative roles is: one role file, one contract, one genre file, at most two technique files. listener-panel is allowed three persona files; challenger is allowed the originality policy, the blocked-targets list, and the cliché list. The memory lessons block (§14) and the originality clause (§15) are exempt from counting. audit_agent_prompt.py enforces the manifest (§11).

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "defaults": { "roles": 1, "contracts": 1, "genres": 1, "techniques": 2, "personas": 0, "rubrics": 0, "shared": 0 },
  "roles": {
    "listener-panel": { "personas": 3, "genres": 0, "techniques": 0 },
    "challenger":     { "shared": 3, "genres": 0, "techniques": 0 },
    "hook-judge":     { "rubrics": 1, "techniques": 1 },
    "music-judge":    { "rubrics": 1, "techniques": 1 },
    "prosody-judge":  { "rubrics": 1, "techniques": 1 },
    "structure-judge":{ "rubrics": 1, "techniques": 1 }
  },
  "exempt_blocks": ["originality-policy", "memory-lessons"]
}

Shared references (music-team/references/shared/) are the only files the orchestrator itself may load, and only the doctrine, stage-gate table, routing matrix, and config schema.

flowchart LR
    L0[L0 marketplace.json<br/>names + triggers] --> L1[L1 SKILL.md<br/>orchestrator or worker]
    L1 --> L2[L2 role file +<br/>output contract]
    L2 --> L3[L3 genre / technique /<br/>persona / rubric per allowance]
    L3 --> SA((sub-agent<br/>isolated context))
    SA -->|artifact only| L1

│       ├── artifact-formats.md     # lyric sheet, chord chart, ABC, production brief, challenge report specs
│       ├── cliche-list.txt
│       └── glossary.md
├── skills/
│   ├── music-flow/                  # Tier A — orchestrator
│   ├── music-brief/                 # Tier C — intake + concept; writes config if absent
│   ├── lyricist/                   # Tier B — roles: hook-writer, verse-writer, lyric-editor
│   ├── composer/                   # Tier B — roles: harmony, melody, groove
│   ├── arranger/                   # Tier B — roles: instrumentation, dynamics, production-brief
│   ├── song-critic/                # Tier B — roles: hook-judge, prosody-judge, structure-judge, music-judge, listener-panel, challenger

    │   ├── briefs/                 # one brief per routing row (8) for detection tests
    │   ├── songs/<type>/           # one complete passing .song/<slug>/ artifact set per song type

Each skills/<name>/ directory follows:

skills/<name>/
├── SKILL.md
└── references/
    ├── roles/            # one file per role (L2)
    ├── contracts/        # output contracts, one per task type (L2)
    ├── genres/           # one file per genre (L3)
    ├── techniques/       # craft techniques (L3)
    ├── rubrics/          # song-critic only (L3)
    ├── personas/         # song-critic only (L3)
    └── agent-prompts/    # sub-agent prompt templates per task type

Agent definitions. agents/*.md are thin named agents (frontmatter name, description, tools) whose body is the Appendix B skeleton. The orchestrator dispatches with subagent_type set to one of them so the SubagentStop matcher in §11 fires. Role and reference content is still injected per dispatch; the agent file carries no craft knowledge.

docs.title: 6. The music-flow Pipeline
docs.text:
Seven stages, mirroring delivery-flow's count so the mental model transfers. Which stages run, and at what depth, is decided by the routing matrix in §7. Every gate names its script and its config threshold; the exact rules are written in references/shared/stage-gates.md (W0-2) and implemented by the scripts in §12.

# Stage Owner role(s) Critic role Produces Gate script(s) Threshold key 1 Brief music-brief (inline) — brief.md; .song/config.yml if absent brief validation (theme required; song type detected; language set) — 2 Concept lyricist:hook-writer hook-judge concept.md (title, hook line, central image, arc) cliche_scan.py; prosody_check.py --hook quality.cliche_max_per_100_words, quality.hook_max_syllables 3 Structure composer:groove structure-judge structure.md (form, bar counts, tempo, key, time sig, per-section meter spec) structure_check.py form template in techniques/form-templates.md 4 Lyrics lyricist:verse-writer then lyricist:lyric-editor prosody-judge lyrics.md prosody_check.py, rhyme_check.py, cliche_scan.py quality.prosody_tolerance, quality.slant_rhyme_allowed, quality.cliche_max_per_100_words 5 Music composer:harmony then composer:melody music-judge chords.md, melody.abc chord_tools.py, abc_validate.py quality.diatonic_min_ratio, quality.max_melodic_leap, quality.vocal_range 6 Arrangement arranger (instrumentation → dynamics → production-brief) structure-judge arrangement.md, production-brief.md arrangement_check.py, structure_check.py --consistency quality.energy_curve 7 Release song-critic:listener-panel → song-critic:challenger → music-release — panel-report.md, challenge-report.md, package/ challenge_gate.py, resemblance_check.py (when corpus configured) originality.ngram_max_overlap

docs.title: Stage execution protocol (identical for every stage)
docs.text:
1. Orchestrator reads .song/config.yml (created in Stage 1 if absent) and .song/<slug>/state.json.
  2. Orchestrator builds a sub-agent prompt from the worker's agent-prompts/<task>.md template, embedding only the files permitted by the allowance manifest, and dispatches with subagent_type set to the matching agents/*.md definition.
  3. Sub-agent writes the artifact to .song/<slug>/<artifact> and returns the Appendix B hand-back (first line SKILL_LOADED:, then STATUS / ARTIFACT / SUMMARY).
  4. Gate decision (single runner). The orchestrator reads state.json.gates[<stage>]. If the SubagentStop hook pre-populated it in this dispatch and the recorded artifact_sha256 matches the artifact on disk, the orchestrator reuses that result; otherwise (hook disabled, crashed, standalone invocation, or hash mismatch) it runs the gate script(s) itself via gate_common.py and writes the result. Either way this step is the only gate decision point. On FAIL it dispatches the stage's critic role with the script output as evidence, then re-dispatches the worker with the critique, incrementing state.json.loops_used[<stage>]. On SKIPPED (non-English gates) it proceeds as PASS and logs the skip.
  5. On reaching loops.<stage>, apply escalation.on_loop_exhaustion:
  6. ask_user: show the last three attempts and the gate diff; the user picks accept, override (recorded in state.json.gate_overrides[] and decisions.md), or supply guidance (resets the stage counter once).
  7. accept_best: keep the attempt with the best gate metrics, record accepted_best: true for the stage, proceed.
  8. fail: stop the run and write state.json.status = "failed".
  9. Orchestrator updates state.json and proceeds to the next stage the routing matrix allows.

Release loop semantics. A Stage 7b BLOCKER returns to Stage 4 (or Stage 5 if the blocker is musical). Each return increments loops_used.release and resets loops_used.lyrics (or .music) to zero. When loops_used.release reaches loops.release, escalation.on_blocker applies with the same three policies.

docs.text:
Documented in references/shared/song-types.md, which mirrors delivery-team's project-types.md. Detection runs in Stage 1 from the brief text and is logged; routing.force_type in config pins it (banner announced each run). Both this table and the orchestrator derive from the matrix below; there is no second routing table.

Legend: F full stage with loops · L light (single dispatch, gate still runs, no critic loop) · I input (artifact supplied by user, validated not generated) · – skipped.

Type Signals 1 Brief 2 Concept 3 Structure 4 Lyrics 5 Music 6 Arrangement 7 Release Notes FULL_SONG default F F F F F F F LYRICS_ONLY "just lyrics", "words only", no chords/melody mentioned F F L F – – L Stage 3 still produces the meter spec that Stage 4 gates need; Release packages lyric sheet only INSTRUMENTAL "instrumental", "no vocals", "beat", "theme music" F L F – F F F Concept produces a motif description instead of a hook; abc_validate.py skips lyric alignment TOPLINE user supplies chords or a track; "write over this", "topline" F F I F L – L Stage 3 derives form and meter spec from the supplied chords; Stage 5 runs melody role only, harmony is validated input REWRITE user supplies an original lyric; "fix", "tighten", "second draft" F – L F – – L Stage 3 infers the meter spec from the input lyric; Stage 4 runs lyric-editor only; originality check runs on the input first JINGLE "jingle", "ad", "30 seconds", brand name present F F F F F L F Hard length cap; form template jingle REVISE existing .song/<slug>/state.json and "make the chorus punchier", "slower bridge", "change the key" – per request per request per request per request per request F Re-enters at the earliest stage the request touches; downstream stages re-run as L unless their artifact is invalidated by structure_check.py --consistency PARODY_ADAPT "parody", "to the tune of", "in the style of " refused One-sentence refusal plus an offer to write an original on the same theme; no .song/<slug>/ directory is created. docs.title: 9. Artifacts and Output Contracts
docs.text:
All artifacts are Markdown or plain-text so hooks can lint them. Specs live in references/shared/artifact-formats.md. Summary:

Artifact Path (.song/<slug>/) Format essentials Brief brief.md YAML front-matter: theme, pov, audience, genre, mood, language, target_length_sec, must_include[], must_avoid[], song_type, user_asserts_original_input Concept concept.md title, hook_line, central_image, arc: [start, turn, end], title_rationale; motif replaces hook_line for INSTRUMENTAL Structure structure.md table: section, label, bars, meter_spec (syllables per line + stress pattern), rhyme_scheme; plus key, mode, bpm, time_sig, form_template. rhyme_scheme letters are scoped per section; x marks an unconstrained line (e.g. AxAx) Lyrics lyrics.md [Verse 1], [Chorus] … tags exactly matching structure.md; one line per lyric line; # comments allowed Chords chords.md per section: Roman numerals + concert chords, one bar per \| cell, e.g. \| I \| V \| vi \| IV \| Melody melody.abc ABC 2.1, one voice, w: lyric lines when lyrics.md exists, K: and M: matching structure.md Arrangement arrangement.md table: section, energy(1-10), instruments_in, instruments_out, texture_note Production brief production-brief.md reference-free language (no "sounds like "), tempo map, vocal treatment, mix priorities Panel report panel-report.md one block per persona: verdict (KEEP / SKIP), top note, one question; majority line at the end Challenge report challenge-report.md parseable severity table: \| severity \| location \| finding \| suggested fix \| with severity ∈ {BLOCKER, MAJOR, MINOR}; challenge_gate.py reads it Package package/ lyric-sheet.md, lead-sheet.abc, song.mid, one-pager.md, release-notes.md State state.json run_id, stage, song_type, status, loops_used{}, gates{<stage>: {status, metrics, violations, artifact_sha256}}, gate_overrides[], accepted_best{}, owners{}, started, updated Active pointer .song/active single line: the slug of the run in progress; written by music-flow at Stage 1 and at REVISE entry; read by hooks Retrospective retrospective.md frontmatter run_id matching state.json.run_id; body per music-memory/references/retrospective-template.md Decisions decisions.md debate outcomes and user overrides, append-only

Output contracts (skills/*/references/contracts/*.md) each specify: required headings, forbidden content (artist names, quoted existing lyrics), max length, and the exact gate script that will be run against the output.

docs.title: 10. Configuration Schema (.song/config.yml v1)
docs.text:
Source of truth: music-team/references/shared/config-schema.md. Extension protocol identical to delivery-team's: bump minor for additive keys, major for breaking, document migration in the schema file.

Creation. music-brief copies .song.config.yml.example to .song/config.yml when the file is absent, announces that it did so, and proceeds. check_config.py only warns at session start; it never creates the file.

schema_version: 1

routing:
  force_type: null            # FULL_SONG | LYRICS_ONLY | INSTRUMENTAL | TOPLINE | REWRITE | JINGLE (REVISE is detected only, never forced)
  default_genre: null         # used when brief omits genre
  default_language: en

quick: false                  # true: every loop cap = 1, on_loop_exhaustion = accept_best, wizard asks <= 2 questions

loops:
  concept: 3
  structure: 2
  lyrics: 4
  music: 3
  arrangement: 2
  release: 2                  # number of 7b -> 4/5 returns allowed before escalation.on_blocker applies

quality:
  cliche_max_per_100_words: 2
  hook_max_syllables: 12
  prosody_tolerance: 0.15     # fraction of stressed-syllable mismatches allowed per section
  slant_rhyme_allowed: true
  diatonic_min_ratio: 0.6     # fraction of chords that must be diatonic
  max_melodic_leap: 12        # semitones
  vocal_range: [55, 79]       # MIDI note numbers, G3..G5 default
  energy_curve: chorus_rising # chorus_rising | strict_rising | free (see stage-gates.md)
  adversarial_lyrics: false   # run challenger after Stage 4 too, not only Stage 7
  listener_panel_size: 3
  genre_overrides: {}         # e.g. hip-hop: { hook_max_syllables: 16, diatonic_min_ratio: 0.4 }

originality:
  resemblance_corpus: []      # OPT-IN: paths to user-supplied lyric files the song must not resemble
  ngram_max_overlap: 0.05     # applied only when resemblance_corpus is non-empty
  block_artist_references: true

escalation:
  on_loop_exhaustion: ask_user   # ask_user | accept_best | fail
  on_blocker: ask_user           # ask_user | accept_best | fail

memory:
  enabled: true
  path: .song/memory/

telemetry:
  enabled: false              # Wave 5 feature

The setup wizard (in music-brief) infers what it can from the brief and asks only what is missing, from this ordered list of at most 6 questions: genre, mood, theme, audience, length, anything-to-avoid. In quick mode it asks at most 2.

docs.title: 11. Hooks
docs.text:
music-team/hooks/hooks.json. All scripts are self-contained stdlib-only Python (no shared lib/ import; the repo .gitignore ignores lib/ directories, which is why delivery-team's hooks/lib/hook_utils.py is absent from git and six delivery-team hooks currently fail at import; a backlog item is noted in Appendix C). Each hook has a unit test that pipes a sample stdin payload. Built with plugin-dev:hook-development loaded. Hook I/O contract follows Claude Code's protocol, not a custom one: read the tool payload from stdin as JSON; exit 0 to allow; exit 2 with the reason on stderr to block; for PreToolUse, a JSON object on stdout with hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision (allow / deny / ask) and permissionDecisionReason. Paths are normalised with pathlib.PurePath(path).as_posix() before any matching so Windows backslash paths behave.

Event Matcher Hook Purpose Wave SessionStart * check_config.py Warn if .song/config.yml missing or schema_version behind; never block, never create 4 PreToolUse Skill prompt hook If music-team:lyricist / composer / arranger is invoked without .song/config.yml, warn (not deny) that gates will not run; "skip pipeline" bypasses 4 PreToolUse Agent audit_agent_prompt.py Deny when: the prompt embeds more references/ files than prompt-allowances.json allows for the named role; the originality clause is missing; or the prompt contains an entry from blocked-targets.txt as a style target. Case-insensitive whole-phrase match 4 PostToolUse Write\|Edit validate_artifacts.py If the normalised path ends with .song/<slug>/lyrics.md, chords.md, melody.abc, structure.md, or arrangement.md: run the matching lint and print findings as hook output. Advisory only (exit 0) 4 SubagentStop lyricist\|composer\|arranger gate_subagent.py Resolve the active slug from .song/active, run the current stage's gate script, and pre-populate state.json.gates[<stage>] with the JSON result plus artifact_sha256. Writes via temp file + atomic rename and touches only gates[]. Advisory: exit 0 always; the orchestrator decides in protocol step 4 4 Stop * prompt hook Read the slug from .song/active. If its state.json has stage >= 7 and status != failed and no retrospective.md beside it carries run_id equal to state.json.run_id, block with "Post-pipeline protocol not completed". A REVISE run gets a new run_id, so a stale retrospective does not satisfy it 4 PreToolUse Skill telemetry.py Skill-load telemetry, copied from delivery-team 5 (optional) PostToolUse Agent verify_skill_load.py Check that the sub-agent's first five output lines contain SKILL_LOADED: and that the listed paths match the dispatched allowance; warn on mismatch 5 (optional)

docs.title: 12. Scripts
docs.text:
All in music-team/scripts/, stdlib-only, python -I-safe. Every gate script imports gate_common.py and honours this contract so tests are uniform:

usage: <script>.py [--config .song/config.yml] [--json] [--genre <g>] <artifact paths...>
exit codes: 0 PASS | 1 FAIL | 2 SKIPPED (gate not applicable, e.g. non-English) | 3 ERROR (unparseable input)
--json stdout schema:
{ "script": "<name>", "status": "PASS|FAIL|SKIPPED|ERROR",
  "thresholds": { "<key>": <value from config or flag> },
  "metrics": { "<name>": <number> },
  "violations": [ { "location": "<section>:<line>", "reason": "<text>", "observed": <v>, "limit": <v> } ] }

Threshold precedence: explicit flag > quality.genre_overrides.<genre> > quality.<key> > built-in default. The exact rules below are the normative text that references/shared/stage-gates.md carries; tests assert them.

Script Input Rule (normative) Used by prosody_check.py lyrics.md, structure.md Syllables: vowel-group count with a 200-entry exception table. Stress: content words (noun/verb/adj/adv by a 300-word function-word stoplist) carry stress on their first syllable unless in the exception table. Per section, mismatch ratio = mismatched stressed positions ÷ positions in meter spec; FAIL if any section > prosody_tolerance. --hook mode counts syllables of concept.md hook line; FAIL if > hook_max_syllables. SKIPPED when language != en Stages 2, 4 rhyme_check.py lyrics.md, structure.md Rhyme = identical final vowel group plus all following consonants. Slant rhyme = identical final vowel group only, or identical final consonant cluster with different vowel. Scheme letters are scoped per section; x = unconstrained line. Within a section, every pair of lines sharing a letter must rhyme (or slant-rhyme when allowed). FAIL on any unmatched pair. SKIPPED when non-English Stage 4 structure_check.py structure.md [+ lyrics.md, chords.md, melody.abc, arrangement.md] Section labels and order must match the named form template; bar counts within the template's min/max; lyric line counts per section must equal meter spec lines. --consistency: key, mode, bpm, time sig identical across all present artifacts; melody pitch range within vocal_range; section lists identical. FAIL on any diff Stages 3, 6, REVISE arrangement_check.py arrangement.md chorus_rising (default): each chorus energy ≥ previous chorus energy; the global maximum occurs in the final chorus or the bridge; the final section energy < global maximum unless the final section is the last chorus; every verse energy < the following chorus energy. strict_rising: non-decreasing until the global maximum, then non-increasing. free: no check Stage 6 chord_tools.py chords.md, key from structure.md Parse Roman numerals; diatonic ratio = diatonic chords ÷ all chords; FAIL if < diatonic_min_ratio. Emits concert-pitch spellings and warns (not fails) on parallel-fifth voice leading between adjacent root-position triads and on a section ending without a cadence Stage 5 abc_validate.py melody.abc [+ lyrics.md] Must parse as ABC 2.1 with single V:; K: and M: must equal structure.md; no interval > max_melodic_leap; all pitches within vocal_range. When lyrics.md exists, lyric alignment applies ABC 2.1 w: rules: - splits a word into syllable tokens, _ extends the previous syllable over the next note (no new token), * skips a note, ~ joins two words into one token, \| advances to the next bar; after applying them, syllable tokens + _ extensions + * skips must equal the number of non-rest note heads in the corresponding bars, and the de-hyphenated w: text per section must equal the lyrics.md section text. Alignment is skipped for INSTRUMENTAL Stage 5 midi_export.py melody.abc, chords.md Writes a type-1 MIDI file: track 0 tempo/time sig, track 1 melody, track 2 block chords one per bar. Round-trip test parses the header and both track lengths Stage 7 cliche_scan.py any lyric or concept text Case-insensitive whole-phrase hits against cliche-list.txt per 100 words; FAIL if > cliche_max_per_100_words Stages 2, 4, challenger resemblance_check.py lyric text + originality.resemblance_corpus Word 5-gram overlap ratio = matching 5-grams ÷ total 5-grams; FAIL if > ngram_max_overlap. SKIPPED when the corpus list is empty Stage 7b challenge_gate.py challenge-report.md Parse the severity table; FAIL if any row has severity BLOCKER; ERROR if the table is missing or malformed Stage 7b check_reference_caps.py music-team/**/references/** Every reference file ≤ 150 lines (genre files ≤ 100); files listed as duplicates in CROSS-SKILL-REFERENCES.md must be byte-identical. Plugin-local lint run in CI; does not touch the shared check_skill_budgets.py CI

Unit tests live in tests/unit/test_<script>.py and run with python -I -m unittest discover tests/unit. Each test module covers: one PASS fixture, one FAIL fixture, the SKIPPED path where defined, one ERROR fixture from tests/fixtures/negative/, and a Windows-style path argument. The prosody gold set target is ≥ 90% line-level syllable accuracy and ≥ 85% stress accuracy.

docs.title: 14. Memory and Self-Learning
docs.text:
Pattern copied from .delivery/memory/.

  • music-memory runs after Stage 7 (enforced by the Stop hook). It writes .song/memory/<date>-<slug>.md containing: genre, song type, loops used per stage, which gate failed most, what critique recurred, user overrides, and three "next time" notes.
  • At Stage 1, music-flow reads the last five memory files for the same genre and injects a ≤ 10-line "lessons" block into the Stage 2 and Stage 4 sub-agent prompts. The block is exempt from the allowance manifest and is labelled <!-- memory-lessons --> so the audit hook recognises it.
  • Memory never stores lyric text, only observations about process.

docs.title: 15. Guardrails: Originality and Copyright
docs.text:
Documented verbatim in references/shared/originality-policy.md and embedded in every creative sub-agent prompt. audit_agent_prompt.py denies any Agent prompt missing the clause.

  1. Never reproduce, closely paraphrase, or "write in the exact style of" an identifiable existing song or artist. Genre and era are fine; named artists and song titles as targets are not. blocked-targets.txt is the machine-checked list; the clause covers names not on the list.
  2. PARODY_ADAPT requests are refused with a one-sentence explanation and an offer to write an original song on the same theme.
  3. Production briefs describe sound with technical language, not "sounds like ".
  4. The default originality control is the challenger role, which reports any line it recognises as a well-known lyric as a BLOCKER row that challenge_gate.py catches. resemblance_check.py is an opt-in second control that runs only when the user configures originality.resemblance_corpus; the README says so explicitly.
  5. User-supplied input for REWRITE / TOPLINE must be asserted by the user as their own original work; the wizard asks once and records user_asserts_original_input: true in brief.md.

docs.text: Wave DoD 0 Validator passes; budget CI covers music-team; reference-caps CI runs; every shared reference has frontmatter; stage-gates.md states every rule in §12; cliche-list ≥ 150, blocked-targets ≥ 100 1 Every script honours the gate_common.py contract (--help, --json, --config, exit 0/1/2/3); unit tests pass under python -I -m unittest discover tests/unit; prosody gold accuracy ≥ 90% syllables / ≥ 85% stress; all negative fixtures produce expected JSON 2 Each SKILL.md within budget; every role file ≤ 150 lines; per-story ACs met; LYRICS_ONLY run ships a lyric sheet end-to-end from the pop fixture with no user intervention, in both default and quick mode 3 Music scripts pass unit tests; composer and arranger per-story ACs met; FULL_SONG fixture artifact set passes every gate script when run manually in sequence 4 All six smoke-tested types complete via music-flow, plus REVISE per W4-4; hooks behave per their ACs; Stop hook enforces retrospective per run_id; smoke baseline committed and runner passes 5 All ten genres present in all three worker skills; duplicates byte-identical; blocked-targets ≥ 500; skill-reviewer has no HIGH findings; README examples reproduce; ARCHITECTURE.md supersedes this plan

docs.text: Risk Impact Mitigation Heuristic syllable/stress counting is noisy False gate failures, loop exhaustion Tolerance knob; exception table grows from the gold set; prosody-judge may flag a suspected heuristic false positive in its critique, and the user decides at escalation. Judges never override a gate ABC melody output from a language model is frequently malformed Stage 5 loops abc-notation-primer.md defines the strict subset the validator accepts; abc_validate.py returns line-precise violations fed back into the loop Sub-agents drift into naming artists Policy violation Hook denial via blocked-targets.txt + the clause + challenger BLOCKER + block_artist_references default true Reference library balloons past budgets Context bloat defeats progressive disclosure Plugin-local check_reference_caps.py in CI (150-line cap, 100 for genres); the shared budget script is only extended to walk the plugin, not to lint references Duplicated technique files drift apart Inconsistent craft guidance between skills CROSS-SKILL-REFERENCES.md lists pairs; check_reference_caps.py fails CI on byte difference Genre files become opinionated and stale Poor output in some genres Each genre file carries last_reviewed; fitness review covers them Seven stages feel heavy for a quick lyric Users bypass the pipeline LYRICS_ONLY and REWRITE paths run 3–4 stages; quick mode bounds loops; standalone worker invocation warns rather than denies Smoke baseline is non-deterministic Flaky CI Baseline is a tolerance comparison, not an exact match; it runs on demand, not on every PR

docs.title: 20. Open Questions
docs.text:
Decisions the author took by default; flag if you disagree.

  1. Plugin name music-team (vs. song-creator, songwriter). Chosen for parallelism with delivery-team / hardware-team.
  2. ABC notation as the melody format (vs. MusicXML or MIDI-only). Chosen because it is text, lintable, and representable by a language model; midi_export.py bridges to binary.
  3. Ten launch genres. Expandable; the list is a judgment call.
  4. No audio. Confirmed non-goal; could become a later wave via an external MCP server if one exists.
  5. Standalone worker invocation warns rather than denies (delivery-team denies for implementation skills). Songwriting is lower-stakes than shipping code, so friction is reduced.
  6. English-only gates at v1. Non-English lyrics run with prosody and rhyme gates SKIPPED. A per-language syllable module is the obvious v2 extension point.
  7. Quick mode defaults (loop cap 1, accept_best, ≤ 2 wizard questions). The thresholds are a guess at "casual user patience" and should be tuned from smoke-baseline timing.
  8. Listener panel is advisory, not a gate. Its verdict is shown to the user and recorded; only the challenger and scripts gate release.

docs.title: Appendix A — Example Session Walkthrough
docs.text:
User: "Write me an upbeat indie-pop song about moving to a new city and not knowing anyone yet."

  1. music-flow triggers. .song/config.yml is absent, so music-brief copies it from the example and says so. The wizard infers genre pop (sub-tag indie), mood upbeat, and theme from the brief, and asks the three missing questions (audience: 20s–30s; length: ~3:00; avoid: "no specific city names"). Writes brief.md with language: en, detects FULL_SONG.
  2. Concept: lyricist:hook-writer sub-agent (dispatched as agents/lyricist.md) loads roles/hook-writer.md, contracts/hook.md, genres/pop.md, techniques/hook-craft.md, techniques/prosody.md, the originality clause, and a 6-line memory lessons block. Returns title "Nobody Knows My Name Here (Yet)" with hook line and arc. cliche_scan.py reports 0.9/100 and prosody_check.py --hook counts 9 syllables: PASS.
  3. Structure: composer:groove sets 118 bpm, 4/4, key D major, form template VCVCBC expanded to V1 PC C V2 PC C B C C, meter spec per section. structure_check.py PASS.
  4. Lyrics: verse-writer drafts; prosody_check.py flags a 22% stress mismatch in Verse 2 (tolerance 15%): FAIL. prosody-judge critiques citing the two violation locations; lyric-editor revises; second run 9%: PASS. rhyme_check.py PASS with two slant rhymes allowed.
  5. Music: harmony writes | I | V | vi | IV | verse and a | IV | I | V | V | pre-chorus lift (diatonic ratio 1.0). melody writes ABC with w: lyric alignment. abc_validate.py flags one leap of 14 semitones (limit 12): FAIL; music-judge critiques; one loop; PASS.
  6. Arrangement: energy curve V1 3, PC 5, C 7, V2 4, PC 6, C 8, B 5, C 9, C(out) 9. arrangement_check.py in chorus_rising mode: choruses 7 → 8 → 9 → 9 non-decreasing, global max 9 in the final chorus, every verse below its following chorus: PASS. structure_check.py --consistency PASS.
  7. Release: three personas (casual-radio, playlist-curator, lyric-first) return KEEP / KEEP / SKIP with notes. The challenger's severity table has one MINOR row (bridge rhyme too predictable) and zero BLOCKER rows; challenge_gate.py PASS; resemblance_check.py SKIPPED (no corpus). music-release assembles package/ and exports song.mid. music-memory writes the retrospective; the Stop hook approves.

docs.title: Appendix B — Sub-Agent Prompt Template
docs.text:
Every agent-prompts/*.md follows this skeleton. The orchestrator substitutes the bracketed parts. The body of each agents/*.md definition is this skeleton with no content filled in.

You are the {role} for music-team, working on "{title}" ({genre}, {song_type}).

## Originality policy (verbatim, non-negotiable)
<!-- originality-policy -->
{contents of references/shared/originality-policy.md}

## Your role
{contents of roles/{role}.md}

## Output contract
{contents of contracts/{contract}.md}
Write the artifact to: {artifact_path}

## Genre guidance
{contents of genres/{genre}.md}

## Techniques (per allowance)
{contents of techniques/{t1}.md}
{contents of techniques/{t2}.md}

## Inputs from earlier stages
{brief.md} {structure.md} {previous artifact if revising}

## Critique to address (if any)
{critique text and gate script JSON}

<!-- memory-lessons -->
## Lessons from memory (<=10 lines)
{lessons block}

## Return
Reply in exactly this shape so hooks can parse it:
SKILL_LOADED: <comma-separated list of every references/ path embedded above>
STATUS: DONE | BLOCKED
ARTIFACT: <path written>
SUMMARY: <=15 lines: what you produced and any decision you want the orchestrator to record

docs.title: Hooks Reference
docs.text: The delivery-team plugin installs 7 hooks across 5 event types. Hooks run automatically to enforce pipeline discipline, validate artifacts, and maintain quality.

docs.title: Hook Summary
docs.text: # Hook Event Type Purpose 1 Config Check SessionStart Validate .delivery/config.yml exists and is current 2 Retrospective Enforcement Stop Block session end if pipeline work occurred without retrospective 3 Pipeline Bypass Detection PreToolUse (Skill) Warn when developer/godot/quality invoked outside delivery-flow 4 Agent Prompt Audit PreToolUse (Agent) Audit agent prompts for context isolation compliance 5 GDScript Validation PostToolUse (Write/Edit) Parse-validate .gd files via godot --headless --check-only 6 Skill Load Verification PostToolUse (Agent) Verify SKILL_LOADED signal in agent responses 7 Empirical Validation SubagentStop (developer/godot) Detect runtime-only acceptance criteria

docs.title: 1. Config Check (SessionStart)
docs.text:
Event: SessionStart Matcher: * (all sessions) Type: Command (check_config.py) Timeout: 5 seconds

Runs at the start of every session. Validates that .delivery/config.yml exists and checks its schema version against the current version. Reports warnings if the config is missing, stale, or outdated.

docs.title: 2. Retrospective Enforcement (Stop)
docs.text:
Event: Stop Matcher: * (all sessions) Type: Prompt Timeout: 15 seconds

Checks if the session involved delivery-flow pipeline work. If pipeline work occurred, verifies that:

  1. A retrospective was run
  2. Memory file was written to .delivery/memory/
  3. Defect review was completed (if defects were found)

If the post-pipeline protocol was not completed, the hook blocks the session end with a reason.

Configuration: Controlled by enforcement.retro_frequency and enforcement.retro_skip_allowed in config.

docs.title: 3. Pipeline Bypass Detection (PreToolUse - Skill)
docs.text:
Event: PreToolUse Matcher: Skill Type: Prompt Timeout: 15 seconds

Detects when implementation skills (delivery-team:developer, delivery-team:godot, delivery-team:quality) are invoked for implementation work outside an active delivery pipeline. If no .delivery/config.yml exists, the hook denies the invocation with a message directing the user to start the pipeline first or explicitly skip.

Non-implementation skills (delivery-flow, product-delivery, architect, ui, operations, user-feedback) are always allowed.

docs.title: 4. Agent Prompt Audit (PreToolUse - Agent)
docs.text:
Event: PreToolUse Matcher: Agent Type: Command (audit_agent_prompt.py) Timeout: 10 seconds

Audits agent prompts before they execute. Checks for context isolation compliance — ensures agent prompts do not leak context from other agents or contain information outside their isolated scope.

Configuration: Controlled by pipeline.isolation_audit (off, warn, block).

docs.title: 5. GDScript Validation (PostToolUse - Write/Edit)
docs.text:
Event: PostToolUse Matcher: Write|Edit Type: Command (validate_gdscript.py) Timeout: 15 seconds

After any file is written or edited, checks if the file has a .gd extension. If so, runs godot --headless --check-only to parse-validate the GDScript syntax. Reports errors if the script has syntax issues.

Only activates for .gd files — other file types are ignored.

docs.title: 6. Skill Load Verification (PostToolUse - Agent)
docs.text:
Event: PostToolUse Matcher: Agent Type: Command (verify_skill_load.py) Timeout: 10 seconds

After an agent sub-agent completes, verifies that the response begins with the SKILL_LOADED: <skill-name> signal. This confirms the skill was actually activated rather than the agent proceeding without loading its SKILL.md.

Configuration: Controlled by pipeline.verify_skill_loading (default: true).

docs.title: 7. Empirical Validation (SubagentStop)
docs.text:
Event: SubagentStop Matcher: developer|godot Type: Command (flag_empirical_validation.py) Timeout: 30 seconds

When a developer or godot sub-agent completes, scans the agent's output for acceptance criteria that require runtime validation (visual output, user interaction, API responses, database queries). Flags these criteria as requiring manual or runtime verification rather than code inspection alone.

This prevents acceptance criteria from being incorrectly marked as "verified by inspection" when they require the application to be running.

docs.title: Memory System
docs.text: The delivery pipeline learns from every run. Memory files are stored at .delivery/memory/ and are project-specific.

docs.title: Design Principle: Read Less, Find More
docs.text:
Memory uses a tiered chunked retrieval system — the AI reads only what is relevant, never the entire memory store.

Tier File When Read Content Routing Index memory/index.md Every pipeline start Topic pointers, stage health, hot lessons (~50 lines) Stage Chunks memory/stages/<stage>.md When that stage executes Stage-specific lessons (~100 lines each) Topic Chunks memory/topics/*.md When relevant context needed Cross-cutting lessons by topic Run Archive memory/archive/*.md Deep analysis only Raw run logs (never read in normal execution)

Total reads per stage: 2-3 files maximum.

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
.delivery/memory/
├── index.md                  # Routing index (ALWAYS read first)
├── stages/
│   ├── idea.md               # Lessons for Idea stage
│   ├── refine.md             # Lessons for Refine stage
│   ├── design.md             # Lessons for Design stage
│   ├── architect.md          # Lessons for Architect stage
│   ├── plan.md               # Lessons for Plan stage
│   ├── development.md        # Lessons for Development stage
│   └── uat.md                # Lessons for UAT stage
├── topics/
│   ├── human-preferences.md  # What the user changed at checkpoints
│   ├── team-decisions.md     # Decisions log with context
│   ├── gate-patterns.md      # Which gates fail and why
│   ├── defect-patterns.md    # Defect rates, categories
│   └── project-types.md      # Lessons per project type
└── archive/
    ├── run-2026-03-21-a1b2.md
    └── run-2026-03-25-c3d4.md

docs.title: Routing Index
docs.text:
The index is a compact pointer file that tracks:

  • Stage health: First-try pass rates and average iterations per stage
  • Hot lessons: Top 5 most impactful lessons (injected into ALL agent prompts)
  • Topic pointers: Which chunk files contain relevant lessons for each context

docs.title: What Gets Injected
docs.text:
Every agent prompt receives:

Lessons from past runs on this project (apply these):
- [Hot Lesson 1 — from index.md]
- [Hot Lesson 2 — from index.md]
- [Project type lesson — from topics/project-types.md]

Active decisions to respect:
- [Decision — from topics/team-decisions.md]

docs.title: Stage-Specific Loading
docs.text:
When a stage executes, these additional chunks are loaded based on context:

Condition Additional Chunk Stage has a human checkpoint topics/human-preferences.md Stage involves decisions (Architect, Plan) topics/team-decisions.md Stage first-try pass rate is below 80% topics/gate-patterns.md

docs.title: Memory Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. First run: No memory exists. Pipeline establishes the baseline.
  2. Each run: Pipeline writes lessons to appropriate chunk files after completion (including aborts).
  3. Over time: Stage health improves as lessons are applied. Hot lessons rotate as new patterns emerge.
  4. Archive: Raw run logs are preserved for deep analysis but never loaded during normal execution.

docs.title: Prior Art Analysis
docs.text:
When user-provided specifications, existing designs, or architectural artifacts are present in the input (PRD with architecture decisions, design documents, technical specifications, prior ADRs), the Architect executes a Prior Art Analysis before any design work:

  1. Read and Summarize -- Read all user-provided specs. Summarize what the user has already designed or decided, the scope and boundaries, and key architectural elements.
  2. Classify Each Element -- Produce a classification table categorizing every element as either "Decision Already Made" (Architect must not propose alternatives) or "Open Question" (Architect is free to propose designs).
  3. Build On Existing Design -- Validate feasibility of user decisions, fill gaps for open questions, and map the design to implementation artifacts (C4 diagrams, component breakdowns, data flows).
  4. Deviation Protocol -- Proposing alternatives to existing decisions is only permitted when a specific, documented technical blocker makes the original decision infeasible. The blocker must be concrete and verifiable.

If no user-provided specs exist, this step is skipped entirely.

docs.text: Type What It Does design Complete architecture with components, interactions, data flows, C4 diagrams review Evaluate architecture against quality attributes with severity findings document Write Architecture Decision Record (ADR) evaluate Compare technologies with weighted criteria matrix decompose Break system into services/components with boundaries model Produce C4 diagram descriptions (Mermaid/PlantUML) analyze-quality Analyze quality attributes with measurable scenarios compliance-checklist Produce framework-specific compliance checklist security-requirements Generate security requirements with OWASP mapping incident-response-plan Create IR plan with severity classification privacy-assessment Conduct DPIA with GDPR/CCPA mapping

docs.title: Architecture Guardrails
docs.text:
Every architecture output enforces:

  • Trade-offs must be stated (no "no trade-offs" allowed)
  • NFRs must be quantified ("p99 latency under 200ms", not "fast")
  • Data flows must specify format, protocol, and error handling
  • Security is mandatory (auth, authorization, data protection, audit)
  • Failure modes must be addressed (circuit breakers, retries, fallbacks)
  • Game architectures require performance budgets (frame time, memory, bandwidth)

docs.title: Delivery Flow
docs.text:
Invocation: delivery-team:delivery-flow

The pipeline orchestrator that coordinates the full delivery team through 7 stages. This is the entry point for all structured delivery work.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: The delivery-flow SKILL.md serves as the high-level orchestration guide. Stage sub-flows, agent invocation details, artifact output paths, and DoD Validator Dispatch Templates are defined in references/pipeline-stages.md, which is the single source of truth (SSOT) for stage details. The SKILL.md contains routing and orchestration context; when executing a stage, the orchestrator always loads the full definition from pipeline-stages.md.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
• Coordinates 11 specialized skills through a 7-stage pipeline
  • Auto-detects project type and routes through appropriate stages
  • Runs quality gates with multi-role Definition of Done validation
  • Self-corrects when validation fails (max 3 iterations per stage)
  • Learns from every run via self-learning memory
  • Supports 6 collaboration patterns for structured quality assurance
  • Manages alias themes for agent personality injection
  • Surfaces active theme in user-facing output (stage announcements, checkpoint summaries, stage transitions) while preserving neutrality in all internal routing surfaces (state files, signals, agent prompts, DoD validators)

docs.title: How to Trigger
docs.text:
Say any of:

  • "start a new feature"
  • "delivery pipeline"
  • "new project"
  • "greenfield"
  • "bug fix"
  • "start delivery"
  • "run pipeline"

docs.title: Setup Wizard
docs.text:
Before the pipeline runs, it checks for .delivery/config.yml. If none exists, the setup wizard launches. Options:

  • Full wizard: 9+ questions covering project type, tech stack, team size, deployment, risk tolerance, compliance, checkpoints, patterns, and personas
  • Quick start: 3 questions — what you are building, language/framework, strictness level

docs.title: Pipeline Phases
docs.text:
1. Phase 0: Setup — Config detection, state resume check, wizard if needed
  2. Phase 1: Type Detection — Auto-detect project type from user input
  3. Phase 2: Memory Retrieval — Load lessons from previous runs
  4. Phase 3: Stage Routing — Determine which stages run and at what depth
  5. Phase 4: Execution — Execute each active stage with the protocol below

docs.title: Per-Stage Protocol
docs.text:
For each active stage:

  1. Announce the stage with purpose
  2. Load stage memory from chunked topic files
  3. Load stage definition from pipeline-stages reference
  4. Invoke primary agent with the Agent Invocation Template
  5. Run collaboration patterns (evaluator-optimizer, adversarial review, etc.)
  6. Run DoD validation — all validators must say DONE
  7. Self-correct if validation fails (route feedback, re-invoke, re-validate)
  8. Human checkpoint if configured for this stage
  9. Update state and advance to next stage

docs.title: Two-Channel Communication
docs.text:
• Signal channel: STATUS, file paths, summaries (max 200 chars) — for routing decisions
  • Artifact channel: File contents written to disk — the orchestrator passes paths, never content

docs.title: State Persistence
docs.text:
Pipeline state is persisted in .delivery/state.md. If a session is interrupted:

  • Resume: Load config from snapshot, skip completed stages
  • Restart: Archive old state, start fresh
  • Abandon: Delete state file

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
User: "Start a new feature — add search to our API"

Pipeline detects: FEATURE
Stages: Idea (full), Refine (full), Design (full), Architect (light),
        Plan (full), Dev (full), UAT (full)
Checkpoints: Refine, UAT

Stage 1: Product Owner captures idea brief
Stage 2: Product Owner writes PRD with stories and ACs
  [Checkpoint: User reviews PRD]
Stage 3: UX Designer creates user flows
Stage 4: Architect designs search architecture (light depth)
Stage 5: Scrum Master creates sprint plan
Stage 6: Developer implements each story
Stage 7: QA runs acceptance tests, personas test the feature
  [Checkpoint: User accepts or rejects]

docs.title: Presentation
docs.text:
Invocation: delivery-team:presentation

Presentation Composer that assembles team contributions into cohesive presentations through a 6-step collaboration flow.

docs.title: Design Principle
docs.text: The Composer is a mini-orchestrator, not a content creator. It assembles contributions from delivery team roles (PO, Data Analyst, Developer, Architect, QA) into a cohesive presentation. Each contributing role loads its own skill. The Composer shapes tone, flow, density, and format.

docs.title: How to Trigger
docs.text:
• "create presentation", "sprint review", "sprint demo"
  • "pitch", "propose", "sell this feature"
  • "status update", "executive update"
  • "technical presentation", "deep dive"
  • "investor pitch", "roadmap", "product demo"
  • "onboarding", "retro summary"

docs.title: Presentation Types
docs.text: Type When to Use Sprint Review End of sprint — what was delivered Feature Pitch Proposing a new feature Stakeholder Update Progress report for executives Technical Deep-Dive Architecture or implementation overview Investor Pitch Fundraising or investment presentation Roadmap Quarterly plan or what is coming next Product Demo Showcase completed features Onboarding Project handoff or team orientation Retrospective Summary What the team learned

docs.title: 6-Step Flow
docs.text:
1. Assemble — Identify type, contributing roles, and source artifacts
  2. Content Gate — Verify source artifacts exist and are sufficient
  3. Draft — Contributing roles produce domain-specific content sections
  4. Compose — Editorial passes: emphasis, cutting, audience framing, narrative tension
  5. Review Gate — Technical Writer (and optionally UX) review for quality
  6. User Review — User reviews and approves the final presentation

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text:
• Structured Markdown (default)
  • Marp — Markdown-based slide decks
  • Paste-Ready — Formatted for copy-paste into slide tools
  • PPTX — PowerPoint output with configurable template and branding

docs.title: Light Mode
docs.text:
Reduces sub-agent dispatch for simpler presentation types:

Config Value Behavior auto (default) Light mode when 3 or fewer contributing roles always Light mode for all types never Full mode always

Override per-request: present --full or present --light

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
User: "Create a sprint review for what we delivered"

Type: Sprint Review (auto-detected)
Contributing roles: PO (what was delivered), Developer (technical details),
                    QA (test results), Data Analyst (metrics)

Output: Structured presentation with slides covering deliverables,
        technical highlights, quality metrics, and next steps

docs.title: Narrative Intelligence
docs.text:
Step 4 (Compose) runs four sequential editorial passes that transform slide content. Order is strict: Emphasis > Cutting > Framing > Tension. Each pass can be individually disabled via config.

Pass Config Key Effect Emphasis Selection presentation.narrative.emphasis Reorders slides so highest-impact content leads (data-backed results first, user impact over technical achievement) Information Cutting presentation.narrative.cutting Removes or merges slides that do not earn their place (no data + no decision = cut candidate) Audience-Specific Framing presentation.narrative.framing Restructures the argument within each slide based on audience values (investor, executive, technical, client-facing, casual) Narrative Tension presentation.narrative.tension Positions the climax slide at the 60-70% point for maximum impact (requires 6+ slides)

Step 4 never degrades -- all enabled editorial passes run at full depth regardless of light mode or threshold status.

Invocation: delivery-team:user-feedback

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:

  3. Spawn each persona independently — each is a separate sub-agent with only its profile

Personas never see each other's feedback. This independence produces diverse perspectives.

docs.title: Collaboration Patterns
docs.text: The delivery pipeline uses 6 structured collaboration patterns to ensure quality. Patterns are configurable per project — enable or disable them in .delivery/config.yml under pipeline.collaboration_patterns.

docs.title: Pattern Summary
docs.text: Pattern When Used Purpose Evaluator-Optimizer After every stage artifact Catch quality issues before DoD Adversarial Review Requirements, architecture, plans Challenge assumptions and find blind spots Review Board Go/no-go and multi-domain decisions Multiple expert perspectives Decision Ownership Mid-stage domain boundary questions Route to the right expert Debate Technology or architecture trade-offs Structured argumentation Consensus Cross-team alignment Mutual agreement on shared commitments

docs.title: 1. Evaluator-Optimizer Loop
docs.text:
The first quality pass after every stage produces an artifact.

How it works:

  1. Primary agent produces the artifact
  2. Evaluator agent reviews against quality gate criteria (PASS/FAIL per criterion)
  3. If any criteria fail: route back to primary agent with findings
  4. Primary agent revises, addressing each failure
  5. Re-evaluate. Maximum 3 iterations.
  6. If still failing after max iterations: escalate to user

The evaluator is intentionally a separate agent from the producer. The separation of roles — produce vs. evaluate — with distinct prompts produces meaningfully better results than self-review.

docs.title: 2. Adversarial Review (Red Team)
docs.text:
Challenges assumptions, finds blind spots, and stress-tests completeness.

Used at:

  • Stage 2 (Refine): Challenge requirements completeness and hidden assumptions
  • Stage 4 (Architect): Challenge design decisions, trade-offs, and security posture
  • Stage 5 (Plan): Challenge estimates, risk assessments, and capacity assumptions

How it works:

  1. Artifact has passed the evaluator-optimizer loop
  2. Challenger agent receives ONLY the artifact (strict isolation — no production context)
  3. Challenger produces: challenged assumptions, missing edge cases, alternative approaches, unaddressed risks, and a confidence rating (1-5)
  4. If confidence is 2 or below: immediate escalation to user
  5. If confidence is 3-5: primary agent addresses each challenge

Confidence scale:

Rating Meaning 5 Production-ready, minor suggestions only 4 Minor concerns, addressable without rework 3 Moderate concerns, direction is sound 2 Significant concerns, major revision needed — ESCALATE 1 Fundamental issues, reconsider entirely — ESCALATE

docs.title: 3. Multi-Perspective Review Board
docs.text:
Multiple expert perspectives for high-stakes decisions.

Used for: Go/no-go decisions, cross-domain concerns where multiple specialists must weigh in.

How it works: Multiple role-specific validators review the same artifact independently and in parallel. All must approve for the decision to proceed.

docs.title: 4. Decision Ownership Routing
docs.text:
Routes mid-stage questions to the right expert.

Used for: Questions that cross domain boundaries during stage execution. Instead of the current agent guessing, the question is routed to the domain owner (e.g., security questions to the Security Architect, data questions to the Data Architect).

docs.title: 5. Debate
docs.text:
Structured argumentation for contested decisions.

Used for: Technology or architecture trade-offs where two valid options exist. Each side presents its case with evidence, and the debate produces a reasoned decision with documented trade-offs.

docs.title: 6. Consensus
docs.text:
Mutual agreement for shared commitments.

Used for: Sprint plans, release scope, and cross-team alignment where buy-in from all parties is required. The consensus pattern ensures all relevant roles agree before proceeding.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Control which patterns run via .delivery/config.yml:

pipeline:
  collaboration_patterns:
    - evaluator-optimizer
    - adversarial
    - review-board
    - debate
    - consensus
    - decision-routing

The Quick Start strictness levels set these automatically:

Level Patterns Enabled Prototype evaluator-optimizer only Standard evaluator-optimizer, adversarial, decision-routing Strict All 6 patterns
